author: Grimm1095
title: Just another lie!!!
content:
Castle Busters is fun, but the way it presents its PvP feels misleading.

The game gives the impression that you are playing another person live. I tested this by leaving the app in the middle of a match and coming back later. The match resumed at the exact same point with the exact same time remaining. Nothing had continued while I was gone.

That raises a serious question about whether these are actually live opponents at all, or whether the game is using bots, simulated opponents, or player profiles controlled by AI.

If matches are not truly live, the developers should say so clearly. Players should not be led to believe they are competing against another person in real time if that is not what is actually happening.

The fix is simple: be transparent about bots and add a genuine live PvP mode where both players are actually connected and playing each other at the same time.

The game has a lot of potential, but competitive games depend on trust. Tell players what they are actually playing against.

author: Donovan Again
title: The new characters make no sense
content:
I really don’t understand what they were thinking with the new character designs. The old characters actually looked like what they did. If a character fired missiles, it looked like a character that fired missiles. You could look at your character and immediately have an idea of what kind of attack you were about to use.

Now it feels almost 180 degrees backwards. The characters have almost nothing visually to do with their abilities. I’m looking at some strange fantasy character trying to remember if this one fires missiles, throws poison, explodes, or does something else. Why would you make something that was easy to recognize harder to recognize?

What really bothers me is that they tested these characters on a smaller group first, and players were already complaining that they couldn’t tell the characters apart and that the old designs represented their abilities better. Then they rolled them out to everyone anyway.

Even the pictures on the App Store are still showing the old characters. If these new characters had been what I saw when I originally downloaded the game, I wouldn’t have downloaded it. If there were a way to completely undo my download and remove the history that I ever had this game, I would.

I don’t care that they changed the artwork. I care that they took characters that made sense and replaced them with characters that don’t tell you anything about what they actually do.

author: Noobpwna
title: Beware: P2W
content:
⭐ 1/5 — Poor Support and a Very Pay-to-Win Experience

I’ve put a significant amount of time into Castle Busters, and unfortunately my experience has reached the point where I can’t recommend it.

After a recent update, more than 300 gems that I had saved simply disappeared from my account. These gems are not easy to earn without spending money — they take a considerable amount of time and farming to accumulate. I contacted customer support, which states that responses are normally provided within 72 hours/three business days. It has now been well over a week, and despite opening multiple tickets, I have received no response or resolution.

The game also feels heavily pay-to-win. Certain characters with significantly stronger abilities appear to be obtainable only by spending real money, putting regular players at an obvious disadvantage.

Even more frustrating, I’ve repeatedly experienced unusual lag, delays, denied boosts, and damage-enhancement abilities failing during matches against players using these premium characters. This happens in the large majority of those matches. I cannot say whether this is intentional or simply a serious balancing/server issue, but from the player’s side, it can make matches feel extremely one-sided and unfair.

My biggest issue is the lack of customer support. If players are expected to spend real money and invest substantial time earning in-game currency, disappearing currency should be investigated promptly. Losing 300+ saved gems after an update and then receiving no response for more than a week is unacceptable.

At this point, Castle Busters comes across as a money grab rather than a game that values its players. Unless you’re prepared to spend money, I would keep your expectations low — and even if you do spend money, don’t expect responsive customer service when something goes wrong.

author: CorkusedIcti
title: Almost Perfect
content:
So first, the good parts. You do not need to spend to win. There is no advantage to being a P2P. There are some units you can buy but I have an 84% win rate and haven’t spent a dime. What ads there are do not intrude, unlike so many other games. Minimal time spent on watching (or not) and some are even fun play breaks. 

The graphics are superb. Smooth, colorful and rich. Play is simple and intuitive; you aim for the other castle and fire. 

Now for the wishlist: Lose the -1 “multplier.” It serves no purpose and detracts from play; who am I up against, the opponent or the game itself?

Also, inconsistent ballistics can be frustrating. At lower levels some inaccuracy is expected but when fully leveled up, that should no longer be an issue. 

None of that is enough to make me stop playing, though, so “almost perfect” is how I’d describe the game.
